newsitem.title: USA: Record rains and flooding swamp New England.
newsitem.headline: Record rains and flooding swamp New England.

text.p: A vicious storm dumped more than a foot (0.348 metre) of rain in parts of New England on Monday and led the governors of Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Maine to declare a state of emergency in flood-ravaged areas.

The storm, which lashed New York and New Jersey on Saturday and which authorities there said claimed four lives, also caused several rivers to overflow their banks in both Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire.

The Taylor River spilled over onto Interstate 95 in Hampton Falls, New Hampshire, reducing the key north-south highway to one-lane, police said. The Neponsett River, which has already overflowed, is expected to crest at 11 feet (3.353 metres), three feet (one metre) over flood stage, on Tuesday.

The Concord and Nashua Rivers were also expected to burst their banks sometime during the evening after torrential rains soaked the area, Massachusetts Emergency Management Agency (MEMA) officials said. Roads and highways throughout the area were closed or flooded out.

Water overspilled several dams in northeast Massachusetts and officials spotted several minor breaches, MEMA spokeswoman Arlene Margolis said. Officials released enough water from one dam to lower a pond's level by 10 inches (25 cm) in hopes of avoiding a total collapse as the fast running water forced people to abandon their cars and turn to canoes to evacuate.
Boston Edison spokesman Mike Monahan said Winchester, a town north of Boston, asked to cut power to its city center because of concerns of overspilling from the nearby dam.

The Red Cross set up eight shelters housing hundreds of residents from various Massachusetts northshore communities that were especially hard hit including Newburyport which was submerged in 12.5 inches (32.25 cm) of rain.
Thousands found their homes flooded, their furniture floating, their cars submerged and streets and roads buried under several feet of water.
"We could use a few more pumps," MEMA's Margolis said, as the high water stretched thin the state's resources.
The National Weather Service said Boston Logan International Airport had 7.92 inches (19.8 cm) of rain. The previous record, of 4.92 inches (12.26 cm) was in October 1895.

Portland, Maine also set a new record for rainfall in a 24-hour period with 7.92 inches (20.1 cm) - breaking a record of 7.75 inches (19.3 cm) in 1991 set by Hurricane Bob, the weather service reported.

Major sections of Boston's subway system were closed when the station at Kenmore Square, an important junction, was under 20 feet (6 metres) of water, a state Emergency Management Agency spokeswoman said. Transportation officials said they did not expect to have the station pumped out until Tuesday at the earliest.

Massachusetts Gov. William Weld declared a state of emergency earlier on Monday and Maine Gov. Angus King followed a few hours later after the brutal storm continued to lash that state's southern coastline. New Hampshire also announced an emergency because of the storms.
The weather service predicted the rain would subside in northern New England later on Monday night and clear through Tuesday. Flooding was expected as rivers continued to crest.
